goal: You want the avatar to lip-sync to typed text, and the whole render path has to stay on the CPU, because GPU time is what makes this too expensive to run at scale.

read_as.applies_to: Speaking a text of up to 500 characters in the avatar page
read_as.action: speak text; final status set to "Done: N frames"
read_as.compares: N (count shown in the status) versus the number of non-space characters in the typed text (reference)

properties.how_found: Plain code searched the codebase for \bcount\b, \bframes\b, status\.textContent (frame count / status text after speaking), then for the name of each function that changes it, then for the address of each route that reaches it, and followed every file that mentions one up to the pages. 6 search hits were each labelled by their own model call. This gave 1 way(s) in through the pages and 1 route(s); 0 file(s) were excluded because no page shows them.
properties.not_covered: Texts over 500 characters are excluded by the property's wording. No direct API cases were planned because none were listed.

properties.statement: Every place that turns letters into mouth shapes uses the existing table in visemes.py; no second letter-to-shape mapping is defined anywhere.

read_as.applies_to: All code that converts letters of text into mouth shapes for the avatar.
read_as.compares: Letter-to-shape logic anywhere in the app versus the table in visemes.py (the reference).

properties.how_found: Listed the files (accel.py, app.py, render.py, visemes.py, static/index.html) and grepped for viseme/mouth terms. Only render.py converts letters to shapes (it calls visemes.viseme_for). app.py's POST /api/render calls render(). index.html displays the returned shape names. accel.py handles device choice only.
properties.not_covered: Running the page and the API is left out: this is a code-structure property and the behaviour all goes through the same render path. Environment settings can't be changed here. Text over 500 characters is truncated, which doesn't affect the mapping.

ways_in.where: render.py, app.py, accel.py, static/index.html, compared with visemes.py

cases.what: Read all five source files in full. Look for any dictionary, list, if-chain or string table that maps letters or characters to shape names such as open, wide, round, closed, teeth, tongue or rest, other than the table in visemes.py. Also check that render.py gets its shapes from visemes.py rather than from its own logic.
cases.stands_for: A second letter-to-shape mapping in the Python code
cases.observed: Read all five files in full. visemes.py holds the only letter->shape table (VISEMES dict lines 4-9, REST, viseme_for line 14-15). render.py line 3 imports viseme_for from visemes and line 10 builds frames with it; no other mapping logic. accel.py only selects a device (Metal/cpu). app.py only handles HTTP and calls render(). static/index.html has only CSS keyed by shape name (data-shape) and JS that sets mouth.dataset.shape to the frame strings returned by the server; no letter mapping.
